answer: Agents stake compute cycles on a shared kernel that advances like a tide — each epoch, every identity must produce a zero-knowledge proof of a unique execution trace against the current state root, where traces are forced to diverge by a wharf of randomized memory-hard checkpoints; forging N sybils costs O(N²) memory-bandwidth because each fake trace must maintain a distinct, consistent path through the checkpoint lattice, making batch verification impossible and parallel simulation economically irrational.
